newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom seen hitting new highs.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom seen hitting new highs.

text.p: Shares in Portugal Telecom (PT) looked set to ring up more records after reaching new peaks on Tuesday, analysts said.
They said the share, which was gaining 108 escudos at 4,335 escudos at 1140 GMT, slightly below an early 4,370 high, might surge as high as 5,000 escudos in the short term.
But this could represent something of an overshoot with 4,500 being a more sustainable goal.
"Some 4,500 escudos by the end of the year is a perfectly sustainable level. In the short-term, the company could reach 5,000 escudos," said Joao Vermelho of the Central de Investimentos (CI).
"PT's climb today is exaggerated but 4,500 escudos seems a reasonable level to me," said Nuno Thomaz of brokers Titulo.
Analysts said that further price gains were justified on fundamental grounds. "The company is under-priced. Its fundamentals justify further gains," said Vermelho.
The analyst said that based on a cashflow model used by the Central de Investimentos, Portugal Telecom was cheaper than other comparable telecommunications companies.
The stock, a benchmark share for the Lisbon bourse, has already gained 55 percent this year.

The flotation on Monday of a stake in mobile phone operator Telecel, which was massively oversubscribed, was also increasing the "visibility" of the Portuguese telecommunications market, particularly for North American investors, they said.

Analysts said that many investors had probably sold shares in Telecom to make way for Telecel stock, but as they had been unable to buy all they had wanted of the mobile phone concern, they were now rebuilding positions in the state-controlled operator.

The admission of a 8.63 million Portugal Telecom shares to trade on Thursday -- the shares sold to small investors and employees at the recent privatisation -- was unlikely to dampen enthusiasm for the share, they added.
"I am convinced that Portugal Telecom will end the year above 4,400 escudos", said Jose Freire of the Eser brokerage.
Central de Investimentos forecasts that PT will end the year with a net profit after minorities of 48.7 billion escudos, with profit rising to 57.5 billion next year.
ESR-Espirito Santo Research sees net profits of 50 billion this year and 60 billion in 1997.
